gumroad_post.title: SRT or VTT? A practical subtitle export checklist
gumroad_post.html:
Already have subtitles, but need a different file format, a transcript or a timing fix? Here is a short checklist for the final export step.

1. Keep an original copy

Work on a duplicate of your existing SRT or WebVTT file. Decide whether the destination needs SRT, VTT, plain text, a timed transcript or a CSV cue sheet. A transcript is useful for reading or notes; a subtitle file keeps the cue timings needed for playback.

2. Check what conversion will preserve

For example, an SRT cue can look like this:

1
00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:03,000
Welcome to the lesson.

In the kit's simple WebVTT export, the same cue becomes:

WEBVTT

00:00:01.000 --> 00:00:03.000
Welcome to the lesson.

Caption Cleanup Kit keeps the cue text and timings, but omits WebVTT notes, styles, regions, cue identifiers and positioning settings. Keep the source if you need those features.

3. Fix a constant timing offset carefully

If every cue starts one second late, a minus-one-second offset may help. If the mismatch grows as the video plays, a single offset will not fix it. Check the start, middle and end against your media. The kit rejects a shift that would put a cue before zero.

4. Review the text and timings

Tidy extra spaces and wrap lines where appropriate. Check overlap, cue order, line length and reading speed. The kit flags possible issues for editing; it does not check the words against your media or certify accessibility.

5. Review the exported batch

Use the review report, spot-check the converted files and test the result in your destination player or editor. Keep your source files alongside the exports.

A small tool for this workflow

I've launched Caption Cleanup Kit for editors, educators and creators working with existing UTF-8 SRT or WebVTT files. Open one self-contained HTML file in a current desktop browser, work offline, and export SRT, VTT, plain transcripts, timed transcripts or CSV cue sheets. Batch export supports up to 100 files, 2 MB per file and 20 MB per batch.

US$9 once, with a quick-start guide and sample files. No installation or subscription is needed, and the workspace does not upload your subtitle files. It edits existing captions; it does not transcribe audio or translate speech.

See the toolkit and download details

reddit.title: I built an offline SRT/VTT toolkit for the final caption export step
reddit.body:
I made Caption Cleanup Kit for a narrow workflow: you already have subtitle files, but need another format, cleaner text, a timing offset or transcripts.

It is a self-contained HTML file that runs in a current desktop browser. It converts SRT ↔ VTT, exports plain/timed transcripts or CSV cue sheets, tidies spaces, wraps lines and applies a timing offset. Batch export handles up to 100 files (2 MB each, 20 MB total) and includes a review report. Subtitle files stay on your device.

A few deliberate limits: it doesn't transcribe audio, translate speech or check words against the video. WebVTT notes, styles, regions, cue identifiers and positioning settings are omitted. Review flags are prompts for editing, not accessibility certification.

It is US$9 once and includes a quick-start guide and sample files. I'm the seller.

https://tiaanbok0.gumroad.com/l/caption-cleanup-kit

If this is part of your workflow, which export do you need most: VTT, SRT, transcripts or CSV?
